# Pataditas

> Pataditas is a private baby kick counter and pregnancy journal for iPhone and Apple Watch, made by Kaelux in Mexico. You tap whenever your baby moves; there is no session to start or stop, and the app groups your taps and notes when 10 movements have been logged within 2 hours. No account, no ads, no tracking. Pataditas is not a medical device and cannot tell whether a baby is well.

Updated: 2026-10-21

## Key facts

- Platforms: iPhone (iOS 26 or later) and a companion Apple Watch app (watchOS 26 or later), live on the App Store.
- Languages (11): English, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, German, French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Simplified Chinese, Dutch and Albanian. The website has full pages in English, Spanish (Mexico) and Brazilian Portuguese.
- Core features: one-tap movement logging (kick, roll or hiccup), 24-hour timeline, contraction timer, Apple Watch app (tap your watch per movement; add it to the watch face or Smart Stack; entries sync with the iPhone through your private iCloud), widgets, Live Activity, Siri and Control Center quick logging, daily reminder, PDF report for your doctor (Pataditas Plus).
- Privacy: no account. Data stays on your iPhone and in your own private iCloud (CloudKit); the developer cannot see it. Anonymous usage statistics are optional (opt-in) and off by default.
- Pricing: counting is free. Two paid options unlock Pataditas Plus (pattern charts, full history, PDF report for your doctor): the one-time Pregnancy Pass (whole pregnancy, no renewals, can be shared with your family; USD 12.99 in the US) or Plus monthly with a 7-day free trial (USD 3.99 in the US). There is no yearly plan. Prices vary by country; purchases are handled by Apple.
- Medical stance: Pataditas records what you feel; it does not diagnose anything and its 10-in-2-hours grouping is the app's own feature, not a health assessment or medical threshold. If your baby moves less than usual, stops moving or the pattern changes, contact your midwife, doctor or maternity unit immediately.

## Guidance note

- Guidance on counting fetal movements differs. Count the Kicks (US) suggests timing how long it takes to feel 10 movements, starting at week 28 (week 26 if higher risk or expecting more than one baby). The NHS (UK) says there is no set number of movements and you do not need to count, but you should get to know your baby's usual pattern; the RCOG patient leaflet also says there is no specific number of normal movements.
- Both say to contact your midwife, doctor or maternity unit (provider) right away if movements reduce, stop or change; the NHS adds to call even in the middle of the night and not to wait until the next day.
- Authorship: written by Luis Angel Lucatero Villanueva, founder of Kaelux, who builds Pataditas. General information, not medical advice. It has not been reviewed by a clinician; medical statements are taken from the sources listed below, last checked 2026-10-21.
